name: Strata 0.2.2
body:
**0.2.2: Gyro on Intel Arc cards and on Macs, faster Gyro on NVIDIA cards, a Main / Helper / Off choice for each graphics card, one models folder for the app and the Terminal, an engine package for the RX 6000 series, an optional API key, and one definition of answer speed.** It also fixes the issues listed below. Each speed claim says what it was measured on, and each new default says whether the answers stay identical. The engine packages are version 0.1.47 (0.2.1 had 0.1.46) and the app is 0.2.2. Update with `strata update` (Terminal), Settings > Update (app), or `UPDATE.bat` / `./update.sh` (source installs).

## What is new

- **Graphics cards can be Main, Helper or Off.** In the app, `strata launch`, setup, the server and Docker, each card gets a role. Main holds the last layers, the draft layer and the final check of every window; a Helper holds a share of the layers and of the expert cache; an Off card is not used and gets no process. The recommended card starts as Main, the others as Helpers, and a card with 8 GB or less starts Off. Short warnings, never refusals, appear for built-in graphics as Main, a card the engine cannot run, too little memory for the chosen setup, and no card at all. A CUDA, HIP or SYCL engine needs a card to start, so with every card Off the server stops in 3 seconds with one plain line; the Mac engine can run without one. Command line: `strata launch --gpu-roles 1=main,0=helper` (cards you do not name are Off), the same flag in setup, `GPU_ROLES` in Docker. On two RTX A4000 the roles gave the expected order (head and draft layer on the Main card, picture reader on the first card), an Off card stayed at 1 MiB with no process, and all-Off stopped as described. Two equal cards now put the lower number on Main, so the engine order is [1, 0] where it was [0, 1]; the cards run at the same speed, so no change in speed is expected. Not tested: the Docker flag, and AMD or Intel cards with roles. Same work: `strata launch` kept replacing the card you picked at install (`"gpu": 1`) with its own pick of GPU 0, which is fixed; the engine log's "GPU 0 / CUDA0" for the first card it is given is now explained by one line from the server; an old AMD `hip_ordinal` no longer overrules the card you name now; and a card list such as `[1, 0]` is passed to the image generator as `1,0`.
- **Gyro runs on Intel Arc (Linux, tested on an Arc A750 only).** The SYCL engine has the trellis kernels (TQ2_T, TQK6, TQK7) and the Hadamard rotation, so Gyro-S and Gyro-M load and answer on an Arc card. Setup lists them like for any card, warns and never refuses when VRAM and RAM together are short, and keeps Gyro's n-gram table on the SSD. On the A750 (8 GB, Ryzen 5 5600X, 62 GB of RAM) Gyro-S reads a 1,406-token prompt at 82 tok/s (40 before the matrix-unit launch took the trellis types, 5 of 5 pairs faster), a 20,000-token prompt at 195 tok/s, and writes 15.8 tok/s with the MTP draft. The card holds 410 of 24,576 experts, so the CPU and the PCIe link carry the decode; for these packs the engine gives the link a larger share (0.48 instead of 0.29, +16% decode, 5 of 5 pairs). On real tensors of both files the kernels equal a host replay of their own arithmetic in every bit, and 7 of 10 test prompts give the same 48 tokens as the CUDA engine (the other three agree for 5 to 9 tokens and then differ at a near tie; first-token KL 1e-4 to 1e-2, top-1 always the same). Details: [GYRO.md](GYRO.md#intel-arc-sycl).
- **A model that is slightly too big gets smaller settings by itself.** When a card is short by a little, setup and `strata launch` now try a 32K, 16K and 8K context, a smaller prompt chunk and a smaller reserve, in that order, and keep anything you chose yourself. Gyro-M on the 8 GB A750 used to stop with no room for a single cached expert; it now starts with a 16K context, reserve 100 and `--prefill 1024` (the estimate was 300 expert slots and the engine got 309), and it answered correctly (Canberra, 391) at 16.6 tok/s. A model that fits keeps its settings. The check is wired into the Intel Arc setup and the Terminal's launch; the app's own fit check is not changed.
- **Gyro-S and Gyro-M run on Apple Silicon Macs.** The Metal engine now has kernels for agentionai's trellis experts (TQ2_T, TQK6, TQK7) and the Hadamard rotation they need, in the decode window and in both prompt paths, and reads the published files unchanged. Setup, the app and `strata launch` list Gyro on a Mac next to the other sizes, never as the default. Gyro-S is 58.5 GB on disk, of which 28.8 GB is the n-gram table that is read from the SSD; its weights need about 38 GB to stay in memory, so a 48 GB Mac holds it and a 32 GB Mac streams the experts. **Measured on a Mac mini M4 with 32 GB:** 9.1 tok/s decode (5 interleaved pairs) and 109 tok/s on a 4K prompt. The Gyro-specific dense-weight tiles gave +5% decode over the generic ones (5 of 5 pairs, same tokens). **Checked:** the decoder equals the format's definition bit for bit on the real tensors, the rotation equals the CPU's bit for bit, and the expert kernels match a double-precision reference to 1e-7 on real experts of Gyro-S and of Gyro-M (read by range requests, since it does not fit this Mac). **KL against the CUDA engine** on the same file (4,995 positions of the quant-quality set, mean KL / top-1): Mac against CUDA GPU experts 0.0207 / 95.5%, Mac against CUDA CPU experts 0.0187 / 95.4%, and the two CUDA runs against each other 0.0186 / 95.8%: the Mac sits at the CUDA engine's own noise level. **Not measured:** Gyro-M end to end, a Mac with 48 GB or more, and the experts' streaming copy for Gyro (it needs 26 GB more disk than the test Mac had). It needs the 0.2.2 Mac engine; an older one refuses the file when it loads, and setup says so.
- **Gyro decodes faster on NVIDIA cards.** The gate/up and down kernels for agentionai's trellis experts now keep the codebook in shared memory and take four rows per warp. On an RTX 3060 (12 GB) Gyro-S went from 54.3 to 62.5 tokens per second (+15%) and Gyro-M from 50.2 to 54.8 (+9%), 5 interleaved pairs each, faster in all of them; prompts are unchanged. The answers are bit for bit the old ones (identity gate on Gyro-S, Gyro-M, Q2_0 and IQ3_XXS), and Q2_0 and IQ3_XXS are not touched. Gyro-S is now about 7% and Gyro-M about 16% behind Q2_0 on that card (16% and 23% before); `STRATA_IQ_STAGE_GRID=0` goes back to the old lookup. Cards of other generations were not measured.
- **An engine package for the RX 6000 series (built, not tested on a real RX 6000 card).** Linux has `rx6000` and Windows has `rdna2`, each with GPU code for gfx1030 and gfx1031 (RX 6800, 6900 and 6950 series, RX 6700 XT). They are offered to a PC whose card reports one of those two and to no other: the RX 7000, RX 9000 and Strix Halo packages are unchanged, and a PC with an RX 7000 or 9000 card next to an RX 6000 card keeps the package it had. The engine runs plain kernels on these cards (RDNA2 has no matrix cores) and plain hipBLAS (hipBLASLt ships no kernels for gfx1030, so there is no tuning table). Setup and the app say once that this package was built and not tested on a real RX 6000 card. What was checked: the Linux package builds, every program in it has code for exactly gfx1030 and gfx1031, the rocBLAS kernel files for both are in it, every library it imports is in the package or belongs to the system, `strata --version` runs, and the whole engine (all targets, tests included) compiles for both. What was not: a model on an RX 6000 card, on either system, and the Windows package itself (the Windows build scripts take the new architecture list, but no Windows `rdna2` package has been built). Earlier reports on these cards came from people who built the engine from source ([docs/AMD_HIP.md](AMD_HIP.md#rdna2-gfx1030)). If something goes wrong, open an issue with the end of `strata-<model>.log`.
- **The CPU expert pool splits per NUMA node on a machine with two NUMA nodes (from the branch behind #3201, not tested on a two-socket machine).** Until now the pool kept its workers on the host thread's socket, because workers on the other socket read the experts across the link and were slower. The split gives each socket its own slice of the pool with its own task counter, and places each socket's half of every CPU-side expert in that socket's memory, so a slice reads local memory only. The reporter measured 59.3 against 54.05 tok/s (+9.7%, and +14% and +11.5% in two earlier sessions) on a dual Xeon Gold 6226 with the IOMMU in passthrough. It starts by itself on Linux when the machine has two NUMA nodes with CPUs and runs only when it can (pinned threads, enough free memory per node); otherwise the pool is exactly what it was and the log says why. **A machine with one NUMA node runs the same code path as 0.2.1:** on an RTX 3060 PC with one node the identity gate (10 prompts, exact prompt checks at 4K and 20K) was identical for IQ3_XXS and Q2_0, and the speed A/B (5 pairs, with a run of the same binary against itself as the noise measure) showed no slowdown. `STRATA_NUMA_POOL=0` turns the split off; `STRATA_NUMA_SPLIT=1` still asks for it. The start-up log says what it did: `NUMA pool on: 2 NUMA nodes found ...` or `NUMA pool off: <reason>`. On Windows the node count is read but the split itself is Linux-only for now. The logic runs in unit tests on made-up two-, three- and four-node machines; we have no two-socket machine, so the placement and the speed on real ones are the reporter's numbers, not ours. Do not wrap the server in `numactl --cpunodebind` or `--membind`: it pulls both halves onto one node. Please send the start-up lines and a decode run with and without `STRATA_NUMA_POOL=0` from a two-socket machine.
- **The API key is optional.** The server, `strata launch`, the Terminal and the app no longer refuse to share without a key. Say so (`--no-api-key`, or `"api_key": "none"` in the server config) and it starts, with one plain warning that anyone who can reach the port can use the model and its tools; a public Cloudflare address gets a stronger one. The Terminal and the app still offer to make a key and do by default. In the app, Remove key now also works while local sharing or the tunnel runs. Fixes the refusals reported in #3198 and #3401. The Terminal part is already in 0.2.1.3.
- **Your own GGUF files load again.** "Use a local GGUF", `strata launch --model-path` and `strata models import` now accept what `setup.py --gguf-dir` always accepted: a folder with the files, the folder above it (a whole Hugging Face download, or an old Strata data folder), or one `.gguf` file. Unsloth sets whose first file holds no tensors, linked files (Hugging Face cache, Ollama) and folders with several sizes work; when a file is unusable, the message names the file and says why. Setup no longer deletes your own file when its checksum differs. The download and prepare steps use plain words, the checksum pass shows its own progress instead of a stuck 99% download bar, the bar no longer jumps to 99% when the last pieces of a parallel download arrive first, and a model folder you pick (a whole drive becomes `D:\Strata`) is accepted by the installer whatever it is called. Reports #3316, #3292, #3190. The Terminal part is already in 0.2.1.3.
- **One models folder for the app and the Terminal.** Each of the two settings files now remembers when the models folder was chosen; the one changed last wins and the other follows. Nothing is moved. A folder picked in the Terminal was not seen by the app before, so the same model could be downloaded twice.
- **Change the models folder in Settings > Storage.** A card shows the folder and offers three choices: move the models there, keep them where they are, or start empty (the old models' settings go to `old-models` inside the install folder, the files stay). A move copies each file to a `.part` name, compares its size and SHA-256 with the source, renames it and only then removes the original; on the same drive it renames, and hard-linked pack files are linked, not copied twice. Stop leaves the files already moved in place and points the settings at them. `strata models move NEW` does the same in the Terminal. If a move is interrupted, the card says so and offers "Finish the move" or "Leave it" (`strata models move --status`, `--resume`, `--leave`; `strata launch` prints one line while a move is unfinished). Checked in a real host with 4.3 GB of test files and in 19 tests; the interrupted-move notice was checked by tests only, and its six texts in the other seven languages were written without a native review.
- **Strix Halo with a card of its own on Linux (Ryzen AI MAX+ and, for example, a Radeon AI PRO R9700).** This follows a report of screen freezes, crashes and "engine stopped" on that pair. We have no such machine, so none of it ran on one. Built-in Radeon graphics is no longer the last stage of a layer split (the last stage holds the head and the final check, so it set the pace), the picture reader leaves it for the card with its own memory, `setup --gpus all` leaves it out when two cards of their own exist, and the engine runs at nice +5 on Linux when the PC has such a chip (`STRATA_ENGINE_NICE=N`, 0 turns it off). PR #3484 (John-Pi) is in with its author: `STRATA_PF_PAD` now applies only where the padded product exists (gfx11), which stops the engine from exiting on its first prompt when a gfx1151 stage and a gfx1201 stage share a process; a second change skips the padded dequantisation on the gfx12 stage. On an integrated GPU the automatic expert cache is sized from the smaller of the GPU's free memory and `MemAvailable` minus max(8 GiB, 8% of RAM), because the GPU's memory is the RAM (`STRATA_UMA_RESERVE_GIB=N`, 0 is the old behaviour; `--expert-cache N` is untouched). The fit check counts such a chip's BIOS carve-out once beside the RAM, and setup says when a BIOS carve-out above 16 GB belongs to a Strix Halo that this run does not use. On an R9700 (Q2_0, fixed gate flags) the identity gate was identical (10 of 10 prompts, exact prompt checks at 4K and 20K) and `STRATA_PF_PAD=1 STRATA_PF_GEMM=1` no longer exits. Not tested: a real Strix Halo plus R9700 on Linux, the unified-memory cache cap, and whether the freeze comes from the engine's queues; reading the code, the engine only opens compute queues. Details: [STRIX_HALO.md](STRIX_HALO.md).
- **The CPU workers say where they run, and you can choose.** The start-up line now lists the logical processors of the CPU workers (`CPU workers on logical processors 2,4,...,30 (15 workers, one per physical core; host on 0)`), and the threads have names (`strata-pool-N`, `strata-host`, `strata-stage`). `--pool-cores`, `STRATA_POOL_CORES` and `"pool_cores"` in the run config (`strata launch --pool-cores`) pin the workers to a list you give; it is experimental and off by default. The question behind it ("the threads only use C0 to C7") came from a Ryzen AI MAX+ 395: the pool was already pinned one worker per physical core there (logical 2, 4, ... 30; in a pool-only test 15 workers read 145.5 GB/s, 8 workers on real cores 94.4 and 8 workers on logical 1 to 8 67.2); what sat on the first 16 logical processors were the threads nobody pins, and pinning the CPU picture encoder made it 7 to 19 times slower on that PC, so it is unchanged. No default placement changed. Identity gate (fixed flags, 10 prompts, exact prompt checks at 4K and 20K) identical on a Xeon box with two RTX A4000 and on an RTX 3060 PC; speed A/B on the Xeon box, 5 pairs, decode 64.90 to 66.40 tok/s (x1.023, 3 of 5 pairs), prompt x0.998, inside the noise. `strata launch` used to drop the notices its flags produce; it shows them now. `--aux-cpus auto` was measured again and stays off by default (decode x1.022, 4 of 5 pairs, inside the noise).
- **One speed number everywhere.** Answer speed is every token the model produced (thinking, answer, tool calls; with MTP the kept tokens) divided by decode time. The chat footer, the monitor, the model API and the server console used different definitions: an agent turn read about 632 tok/s in 0.2.0-beta, then fell to the real 50 to 75 in 0.2.1, and some places divided by the whole request, which reads about half (three real requests: 47.8, 64.8 and 65.9 tok/s by decode time, 20.6, 29.0 and 31.5 over reading plus decode). The footer now shows the last reply's own speed, the popover has a "Prompt reading" row, and the console no longer prints a million tok/s for a one-token reply.
- **`strata bench run`, first real runs.** Run on two test PCs with the 0.2.1 release, it showed that the release archive carried no commit (every run was `nonconforming`), that the drive lookup failed on LVM, that the CUDA runtime was missing from the nvidia-smi 615 output, and that the engine log in the result was empty. All four are fixed, the protocol text now says 2 to 4 minutes for the required part (measured 2:22 and 3:22), and results get a Capped column for answers that stopped at the token limit (7 of 9 performance requests ran into the 512-token limit while still thinking). Package building refuses to make a distributable archive without a commit. The two first complete runs are in `bench/results/2026-10-20-0.2.1-bench/`.
- **Tool calls from a model that writes the opener wrong.** A model that opens a call as `<=NAME>`, `<function:NAME>` or `<NAME>` is read as `<function=NAME>` when NAME is a tool the request declared; a block that still does not read as a call is counted and one line is printed per request (#3441). A call for a tool the request did not declare stays text, before and after `</think>` (#3075). **This changes one behaviour:** a Chat Completions or `/v1/messages` request with no tools can no longer get `tool_calls` back. The Responses route is left as it was, because Codex's compaction request relies on it. Constrained decoding for calls (item 3 of #3441) is not done.
- **After a NaN in a long prompt the request survives (#3465).** When the logits turn non-finite in a prompt window, the retry now reads the whole prompt through the batched path (one line in the server window) instead of failing the request. We could not reproduce the NaN itself on a Tesla P100 with a Broadwell Xeon, an RTX 3060 and a Core Ultra with VNNI turned off (IQ2_XS, IQ3_XXS, IQ3_S, Q2_0, prompts up to 30K), so the cause is still open; the retry was tested with an injected non-finite window. The reporter's debug list is in the issue.
- **The Linux CUDA 12 engine package has Pascal and Volta code again (#3503).** The 0.2.1 package was built for sm_75, 86 and 89 only because the repo held no recipe for it. `packaging/build_cuda_linux.sh` builds it for sm_60, 61, 70, 75, 80, 86 and 89, the packager refuses a CUDA 12 package without sm_60, 61 and 70, and the source Dockerfile takes `CUDA_IMAGE` and `CUDA_ARCHITECTURES`. A package built with it ran an IQ2_XS model on a Tesla P100. The 0.2.2 packages are built with it.
- **HIP queue priming stands aside on a restricted queue count (#3480).** When `GPU_MAX_HW_QUEUES` is 1 or 2, the engine no longer opens its two priming queues and says so in one line (`STRATA_HIP_QUEUE_PRIME=nn` still forces them). It compiles for gfx1201; it was not measured on a gfx12 card.
- **Docker.** An old (0.1.x) volume with `/data/models`, `/data/packs` and `/data/mtp` is moved into `/data/Strata-data` by rename instead of being downloaded and packed again (it used to start a 75 GB download). A card without `--gpus` stops at once with the `--gpus all` hint instead of after minutes of setup. A missing or empty `MODEL_PATH` gets a plain message. Settings that name another image's component folder (a CUDA 12 image on a CUDA 13 volume) are made again, and an engine folder renamed by an update no longer ends in `server_exited` when pictures are on. The terminal stage of the image build no longer needs git (it failed with `FileNotFoundError`); the commit comes in as a build argument, and all five image flavors built. Tested on one RTX 3060 PC with CUDA 12 and CUDA 13 images; no AMD or Intel image and no Docker Desktop.
- **Re-runs do not tune again.** A tuning that found the standard settings already fastest counted as "not tuned", so `strata launch`, the TUI and the Docker entrypoint measured again at every start (20 minutes); it counts as tuned now. In the Terminal a first launch of an installed model took 521 s and the second 13 s on the test PC.
- **Problems with the computer's own setup are repaired or explained, not refused.** If the Windows runtime folder lists another account, Strata locks it down itself instead of stopping. A Documents folder that cannot be used (Controlled folder access, an offline OneDrive) falls back to the Strata home folder and Settings > Storage says so. A port that is taken or reserved gets one sentence with the next step. Local requests ignore a system proxy. File-in-use errors and a full disk say what happened. `strata launch` asks plain questions in a terminal that reports a tty late. `strata update` copes with a slow `--version`, a busy graphics card is not held against an engine, pre-release Control builds hand over correctly, and a wrong PC clock is named as the reason a feed or certificate looks bad. install.sh and install.ps1 give clearer messages (ARM, TLS 1.2, proxy credentials, no `tar.exe`). The Terminal parts are already in 0.2.1.3; the Documents fallback and the port handling are app parts.
- **A stale update notice goes away.** After a version change the app and the Terminal no longer keep showing an offer for a version you already have.
- **Idle GPU time was measured, with no default change.** On a two-card test PC decode leaves 47 to 49% of the card time idle (batch 51%, prompts 24 to 42%), on a one-card PC 5%. Overlap gave +0.3, +2.1 and -0.3% against 2.8% noise; pipeline windows 2 gained 5.4% on code only, cost 5 to 13% with the draft layer on the first card, and `--batch-groups 2` cost 15.3% with 4 chats, so nothing is switched on. Raw numbers are in `bench/results/2026-10-20-0.2.1-idle-gpu/`.
- **The recommended size leaves 5 GB for Windows.** The memory tiers now count RAM + VRAM less 5 GB, so a PC with 32 GB of RAM and a 16 GB card gets the 40 GB tier instead of the 48 GB one, which had it reading part of the model from the SSD (#3425). Every other size is still a choice.


## Faster, with what we measured

Speed numbers are medians of interleaved pairs on the same box, a fresh engine per run; "pairs faster" counts the pairs the new code won. Each change has an off switch.

- **Gyro decodes faster on NVIDIA cards.** The gate/up and down kernels for agentionai's trellis experts now keep the codebook in shared memory and take four rows per warp (8 lanes per row), on every CUDA card above Pascal. On an RTX 3060 (12 GB) Gyro-S went from 53.6 to 62.8 tokens per second (+17%, 4 of 5 pairs) and Gyro-M from 50.6 to 56.1 (+11%, 5 of 5), 5 interleaved pairs each; prompts are unchanged. The answers are bit for bit the old ones (identity gate on Gyro-S, Gyro-M, Q2_0 and IQ3_XXS, with the pinned Gyro files), and Q2_0 and IQ3_XXS are not touched. Against Q2_0 on that card Gyro-S is now about 6% and Gyro-M about 16% slower (18% and 24% before). `STRATA_TQ_SUB8=0` goes back to the old rows, `STRATA_IQ_STAGE_GRID=0` to the old lookup. Only the RTX 3060 was timed for this path.
- **Gyro decodes about 30% faster on a Tesla P100 (compute capability 6.0).** On a P100, Gyro-S ran at about 70% of the speed of the Q2_0 file of similar size: 30 / 36 / 33 tok/s against 41 / 51 / 48 (story / code / facts, median of 5 interleaved pairs, default flags). On compute capability 6.0 the engine now keeps the 4 KB trellis codebook in shared memory, reads the down rows as 8-lane rows, lets each block work on several row chunks, and copies the activations of an expert group to shared memory once per block. Gyro-S now decodes 38.5 / 45.6 / 42.7 tok/s (+30%; every one of 10 reps and 5 of 5 pairs faster), 0.96 / 0.90 / 0.91 of Q2_0. Prompt speed is unchanged: 4096 tokens take 14.0 s and 20000 tokens 62 s, 3 to 5% slower than Q2_0. Answers are the same: the identity gate (10 prompts, 4096- and 20000-token prompt dumps) is identical on the P100 and on an RTX 3060, and Q2_0 on the P100 did not change (0.999 / 0.998 / 1.001). The ready-made CUDA 13 packages have no code for this card; the CUDA 12 packages do. `STRATA_TQ_STAGE=0` turns the path off. Two attempts to speed up the prompt (a faster dp4a in llama.cpp's MMQ kernels, which this card lacks, and a register-tiled MMQ dot) were slower and are not included.

## Fixes from user reports

- **Your own GGUF on the first run (#3507, #3424).** "Use your own GGUF" on the first-run page opened the folder chooser for the Strata data folder, so your GGUF folder became the data folder and the installer downloaded into it again. It now opens the local GGUF page, and preparing your own files never uses their folder as the data folder.
- **Loading stopped for good by a reused PID (#3488).** A marker without a start time counted any later program with the same PID number as our engine, and every load stopped. Such a marker now only blocks for a Python or Strata program, and the engine hash check reads twice before it refuses, with the expected and found hash start in the message.
- **Tuning (#3502, #3490).** A CUDA initialisation failure in a tuning run is no longer recorded as out of memory by the memory-guard line, and a command that passed on the same PC, engine and model is no longer switched off for good by a later failure. Tuning gives up waiting for memory when none is being freed in a minute, instead of waiting ten minutes per candidate, and says how much is free and needed.
- **Smaller fixes of the same round.** A Recycle Bin path is found on Linux too, authored by TheHubUser4860938 (#3501); `--control-vector-layer-range` is written and removed as two entries and an empty Advanced value is no longer a bare flag (#3504); the recommendation says how much of the picked size would be read from the SSD when RAM and VRAM only just reach the tier's floor (#3425); UPDATE.bat and setup fetch the engine from the signed update feed when a release has no flat zip, and the minimum engine is 0.1.46 (#3469, #3437; not tested on a Windows AMD PC); on a card that shares the PC memory (Strix Halo) the Work profile no longer reserves a fifth of the shared pool as graphics memory (#3510).
- **From the issues labelled needs-format.** The app numbers Radeon cards the way HIP does when an integrated GPU is present (#3418). The hardware report counts physical cores, so the Work profile asks for 6 pool workers on an 8-core CPU instead of 12 (#3417; the reporter measured 27.9 against 38.1 tok/s). Three trellis CPU tests skip on a ggml without trellis types, and the ISA guard knows the AVX-512 files (#3358, tests and build only; the memory fault on gfx1011 is not fixed, we have no such card).
- **Small fixes.** `--mtp 2` is no longer checked as a folder (#3298); owner-only checks understand Windows account aliases (#3302, thanks jackbapa); `strata bench` with its own server sets its port (#3188); `calibrate` checks the report folder first (#3187); the CUDA 12.0 and 12.1 build error `__half_as_ushort` (#3368, thanks yudhanjaya, compiled as a snippet with CUDA 12.6 only); the AMD picture reader builds position independent (#3359, not built here); the Mac setup installs cmake and ninja before it builds (#3403); the picture reader recreates its work folder if a temp cleaner removed it (#3370); a list of GPUs such as `"0,1"` is accepted (#3275, thanks MEsfits); `thinking_budget_tokens` is read (#2141) and the Anthropic usage numbers add up to the prompt (#2289, thanks xrip); an engine that cannot start is a 503 with the reason (#2496, thanks devYRPauli); the serve web page no longer scrolls sideways on a phone (#2971, thanks ctr-137; 752 px wide before at a 412 px screen, 412 px after); folders in a Trash or Recycle Bin are not offered as installs (#3410). Ported pull requests keep their authors. Most of these are already in 0.2.1.3.
- **Speculative decoding.** A rare hang of the first verify window on the HIP engine is fixed: about 1 run in 5 on a Strix Halo with IQ3_S stopped after the first window (8 of 41 runs without the fix, 0 of 46 with it). The cause was a GPU launch that waited for a flag the host raised only after the launch returned; on HIP the flag is now raised before the first launch of each graph (`STRATA_VERIFY_EARLY_PLE_FLAG=1` or `0` forces either order; CUDA and SYCL keep their order). Decode speed with the fix is 47.89 against 47.78 tok/s (10 interleaved pairs). A one-token prompt with `--spec` on a native pack never started the speculative loop and decoded 0 tokens; it now decodes 24 tokens with the same ids as `--spec 2`. A `STRATA_SPEC_WATCH=<seconds>` watchdog reports a stalled loop with its stage.

## Already in 0.2.1.1 to 0.2.1.4

These went out as Terminal, Control and engine updates before 0.2.2, so a Terminal user has them; the app gets them with 0.2.2. 0.2.1.1: the Windows engine install survives long paths. 0.2.1.2: on Windows, a Strix Halo (gfx1151) no longer registers the whole expert arena at start (the default start failed with "0 MiB free" and exited), and `strata.exe --version` finds its ROCm libraries without a PATH entry. 0.2.1.3 (Control 0.1.46.2): the Terminal parts of the API key, own GGUF, refusal, small-fix and update-notice items above, and `strata launch --plan` that names your files, says what would be downloaded and says "Nothing to download" when everything is there, a total download label that counts every shard, a plain sentence plus a "still working" line during packing, a stored tuning result that is reused (`--retune` measures again), an interrupted `experts.bin` write that continues at the next layer, and the hand-over: after `strata update` installs a newer Control, the Terminal runs it on the next command. Terminals older than 0.1.46.2 cannot hand over (the code is in the Terminal): reinstall the Terminal once. 0.2.1.4 (Control 0.1.46.3): a Windows PC with an RX 9000 card is no longer given the RX 7000 engine because its graphics chip could not be read (#3456, #3486; with an unknown chip and several HIP builds it asks for the variant, then goes by the GPU name, and never picks by version), and every ranged download answer is checked (206, Content-Range, length, ETag); a file with a wrong SHA-256 is repaired piece by piece instead of deleted. Real test: a 907 MB file through a relay that reset connections, flipped 3 bytes and was killed twice ended with "2 of 28 parts were different and have been written again" and the pinned SHA-256; the 0.2.1 downloader deleted the file on the same input. A 39.8 GB shard went through 64 resets and two kills and matched its SHA-256.

## Known limits

- **RX 6000 series:** the `rx6000` and `rdna2` packages were built, not run on a card; the Windows `rdna2` package has not been built.
- **Two-socket PCs:** the NUMA split was not run on one; the numbers are the reporter's.
- **Gyro on a Mac:** Gyro-M was not run end to end, and a Mac with 48 GB or more was not tried. **Gyro on Intel Arc:** a B-series card, two Arc cards (the second-card helper refuses a Gyro pack and says so) and the xe driver were not tried.
- **Gyro on NVIDIA:** only the RTX 3060 was timed for the new rows; the Tesla P100 path is separate.
- **Strix Halo with a card of its own on Linux:** none of the changes ran on that pair, and the cause of the screen freeze is not confirmed.
- **GPU roles:** the Docker flag and AMD or Intel cards were not tested; a CPU-only choice is allowed with a warning, and the CUDA, HIP and SYCL engines cannot start with it.
- **HIP queue priming (#3480):** not measured on a gfx12 card.
- **Open reports we could not reproduce:** #3465 (the NaN itself), #3489 (a driver fault at a 6400-token chunk: two Linux boxes read a 177K-token prompt cleanly, so the reporter's logs are needed), #3297 and #3443 (gfx1201 stalls under memory pressure, not run).
- **Not fixed:** the `vmm_test` memory fault on gfx1011 (#3358), the Slot-to-pool copy speed (#3321, the reporter has a patch), an NVFP4 token soup on a CPU without AVX-512 (#3328).
- **Package against source speed, #3252:** not reproduced. On the same commit, a Linux CUDA 12 and CUDA 13 package matched a setup-style source build within 1% in decode and in 4K and 20K prompts on an RTX A4000 PC and an RTX 3060 PC (5 pairs each). The one difference left is that the packages build ggml's CPU part for a generic AVX2 CPU; we have no AVX-512 plus NVIDIA machine on Windows to test that.
- **Docker:** no AMD or Intel image was built or run, and no Docker Desktop.

Thanks to baptisterajaut, whose NUMA-split branch the pool is built on; to John-Pi (PR #3484), MEsfits (#3276), xrip (#2140, #2290), devYRPauli (#2497), ctr-137 (#3156), yudhanjaya (#3374), jackbapa (#3302) and TheHubUser4860938 (#3501), whose fixes are in with their names; and to agentionai, whose Gyro work all three Gyro ports build on.

---

Strata is free and open source. If it runs well on your PC, a coffee keeps the work on it going:

<a href="https://buymeacoffee.com/strataengine"><img src="https://cdn.buymeacoffee.com/buttons/v2/default-yellow.png" alt="Buy Me A Coffee" height="50"></a>

name: Strata 0.2.1
body:
**Update 0.2.1.4 (2026-10-21): Terminal 0.1.46.3.** On Windows with an RX 9000 card, updating or installing the engine picked the RX 7000 / Ryzen AI Max build, which then failed its test start. Strata now reads the card from Windows' display adapter list and never switches you to another build on an update. Model downloads are checked piece by piece, and a file with damaged parts is repaired (only the damaged parts are downloaded again) instead of being deleted. The app uses the new version automatically; in the Terminal run `strata update` (from 0.2.1.3 on it switches by itself), or install once more with the install command if you are on an older Terminal.

**Update 0.2.1.3 (2026-10-20): Terminal 0.1.46.2.** Fixes for installing and starting from the Terminal: the Windows runtime-folder permission error ("must be owner-only"), your own GGUF files load again (Unsloth split sets, several sizes in one folder, links), plain names for every download and prepare step, preparing a model continues where it stopped, the API key is optional on a network (with a warning), and `strata update` now switches the Terminal to the new version by itself from this version on. The app uses it automatically. If you use the Terminal, install it once more with the install command above; your models and settings stay.

**Update 0.2.1.2 (2026-10-20): Strix Halo on Windows starts again.** The Windows engine for RX 7000 and Strix Halo (hip-rdna3) did not start on a Strix Halo PC with the normal settings: it stopped with "the embedding buffer failed". Engine 0.1.46.1 fixes it, and `strata.exe --version` now also works when started straight from its folder. In the app, open Settings and choose Update engine; in the Terminal, run `strata update`. The Windows hip-rdna3 installer on this page already has the fixed engine. Other cards and systems are unchanged.

**Update 0.2.1.1 (2026-10-20): Windows Terminal fix.** On Windows with long paths off (the default), the Terminal could not install an AMD engine: "The engine could not be installed. local file operation failed (FileNotFoundError)". The engine is now unpacked into a much shorter folder and with paths Windows accepts at any length, and a path that is still too long gets a plain message. If you use the Terminal on Windows, install it again once with `irm https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata/releases/latest/download/install.ps1 | iex` (your models and settings stay); it installs Terminal 0.1.46.1, and `strata launch` works again. (`strata update` downloads 0.1.46.1 too, but the Terminal on your PATH keeps starting the old version; that is fixed in the next release.) A new install gets it straight away. The app and the engines are unchanged.



---

**0.2.1: a task board in the app, pictures on the Mac and on Intel Arc cards, `strata bench run` with a fixed standard benchmark, faster downloads, Docker images, and your own engine settings are no longer overwritten.** It also fixes the crashes, stuck downloads and GPU-choice bugs reported on 0.2.0-beta. Each new default below says what it was measured on and whether the answers are identical to 0.2.0. The engine packages are version 0.1.46 (0.2.0 had 0.1.45.3) and the update feed has sequence number 102. Update with `strata update` (Terminal), Settings > Update (app), or `UPDATE.bat` / `./update.sh` (source installs).

## Which file to download

| System | Your graphics card | File |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Windows 10 / 11 | NVIDIA RTX, driver 580 or newer | `Strata-0.2.1-windows-cuda13.exe` |
| | NVIDIA, older card or driver older than 580 | `Strata-0.2.1-windows-cuda12.exe` |
| | AMD Radeon RX 9000 series or Radeon AI PRO R9700 | `Strata-0.2.1-windows-hip.exe` |
| | AMD Radeon RX 7000 series or Ryzen AI Max (Strix Halo) | `Strata-0.2.1-windows-hip-rdna3.exe` |
| Linux | NVIDIA RTX, driver 580 or newer | `Strata-0.2.1-linux-nvidia-cuda13.AppImage` |
| | NVIDIA, older card or driver older than 580 | `Strata-0.2.1-linux-nvidia-cuda12.AppImage` |
| | AMD Radeon RX 9000 series or Radeon AI PRO R9700 | `Strata-0.2.1-linux-amd-rx9070.AppImage` |
| | AMD Radeon RX 7000 series | `Strata-0.2.1-linux-amd-rx7900.AppImage` |
| | AMD Ryzen AI Max (Strix Halo) | `Strata-0.2.1-linux-amd-strixhalo.AppImage` |
| Mac | Apple silicon, macOS 15 or newer | `Strata-0.2.1-mac.dmg` (signed and notarised by Apple) |

The Terminal installs with one line and picks its engine by itself (`curl -fsSL https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata/releases/latest/download/install.sh | sh`, or `irm https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata/releases/latest/download/install.ps1 | iex` on Windows). The other files in this release are the engine and Terminal packages, the signed update feed and the in-app update files; you do not need to download them. Docker images are separate (below).

## What is new

- **A task board in the app.** On the Tasks screen, a Schedule | Board switch shows your scheduled tasks and loops as a board: what is running, what is waiting for your approval (from every chat), and what failed. Each run has one plain line, only the newest problem of a task is shown, and a problem can be dismissed. The sidebar shows how many tasks need you. All eight app languages are translated.
- **Pictures on the Mac.** The Mac app and Terminal now read pictures by default. The reader runs on the Mac's GPU (Metal), built into `strata-vision` and signed with the app. Measured on an M4 Mac: a 260-token picture 0.45 s on the GPU reader against 50.7 s on the CPU, a 972-token picture 2.4 s against 194 s; the GPU reader takes about 1.2 GB of memory. On the 972-token picture 8 of 972 picture tokens differ from the CPU reader (cosine down to 0.48, in the text area); the answers were correct. `--vision cpu` is still there and warns that it takes about 50 seconds per picture.
- **Pictures on Intel Arc cards.** Alchemist cards (A-series) read pictures by default through the CPU reader; Battlemage (B-series) stays opt-in (see Known limits). A new GPU picture reader for SYCL (`--vision gpu`) takes 0.16 s per picture on an A750 against 1.73 s on the CPU (its picture embeddings equal the CPU reader's to a cosine of 0.9959 to 0.9999). Ten varied pictures and a multi-picture chat all passed on the A750.
- **`strata bench run` runs the standard benchmark.** The default suite is `standard-v1`: fixed request files (34 of them, with a checksum list) in the Terminal archive, a scorer, a validator and a report that leaves out personal data. The Terminal archive now carries its commit, because a run without one does not count. The protocol text in `docs/BENCHMARK_PROTOCOL.md` is still a draft. See `docs/COMMUNITY_BENCHMARKS.md` for how to send a result.
- **Faster downloads.** Big model files come over 16 connections with several pieces per request (0.2.0 used 8 connections and a new connection for every piece). On the test PC, from Hugging Face, three interleaved pairs: 68.6 / 65.9 / 70.6 MB/s before, 74.4 / 74.8 / 74.9 MB/s now (+9%; the line itself tops out near 75 to 85 MB/s). The fetch of the draft layer (MTP) went from 25.0 / 28.1 / 37.6 MB/s to 47.4 / 50.5 / 52.2 MB/s, and its file list from 28 s to 4.6 s. ModelScope downloads, whose server reports no file length, now use several connections too. The files are the same and are still checked against their pinned SHA-256.
- **Docker images.** Ready-made images for `ghcr.io/niko1221/strata:0.2.1-<flavor>`: `cuda13`, `cuda12`, `rocm-gfx120x` (RX 9000, R9700), `rocm-gfx110x` (RX 7000) and `rocm-gfx1151` (Strix Halo). They are built from the signed release packages by the repository's workflow. The start-up test passed on an RTX A4000 (cuda13 and cuda12) and on a Radeon AI PRO R9700 (rocm-gfx120x); the gfx110x and gfx1151 images were built but not run on a card. There is no Intel image yet. See `docs/DOCKER.md`. The workflow starts after this release is published, because it reads the release's own files, so the images appear a few hours later.
- **Your own engine settings stay.** The app and setup used to rewrite the run config on every Load. Options you set by hand (`--vram-reserve-mib`, control vectors, any option setup does not choose itself) are now kept in `user_args`, and what you set wins over what the app generates. See Fixes.
- **Draft layer (MTP) switch.** Settings > Expert has a Draft layer (MTP) on/off per model, and `strata launch --mtp on|off` does the same. A picture-off choice and a custom context size stick across loads.
- **Fit checks count the draft layer.** With MTP on, the draft layer takes about 1 GB of graphics memory; the model fit check and the expert-cache sizing now count it.
- **The model page shows the engine's own pick for your PC** (the memory tiers of 0.2.0), with Gyro-M named as the other choice at 40 GB.
- **The chat footer speed is the writing speed.** It divides output tokens by decode time, so a tool-call turn no longer shows "632 tok/s" when the engine ran at 50 to 75.
- **A wrong download says so.** An installer for another make of graphics card (an AMD build on an NVIDIA PC) tells you in plain words which file to get and does not unpack its engine. An installed engine with no model loaded is no longer reported as "No Strata engine".
- **Terminal.** A model that is already on disk says "already downloaded". `strata monitor` finds a running `strata launch` without `--url`.
- **The standard AMD packages carry the hipBLASLt tuning tables** and the engine start picks the one for the card (see New defaults for when it is used).

## New defaults, with what we measured

Speed numbers are medians of interleaved pairs on the same box, a fresh engine per run; "pairs faster" counts the pairs the new default won. Each default has an off switch.

- **Mini PCs with a Radeon 780M (gfx1103), Linux: the matrix-core prompt set is on.** Measured on a Ryzen 7 8745HS with a Radeon 780M, 60 GB DDR5, Linux kernel 7.0.0-38, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next Q2_0 with MTP, 6 interleaved pairs: a 1K prompt 98.5 to 157.3 tok/s (x1.60, 6 of 6 pairs), a 4K prompt 115.1 to 233.3 (x2.03, 6 of 6), decode unchanged (x0.999 and x1.000). The greedy token ids equal the old default's in every pair (6 of 6, and 5 of 5 in the final build). Same answers, as far as the ids show. `STRATA_IGPU_PROMPT_SET=0` turns it off. It applies to the 780M and 760M on Linux only; 880M, 890M, Strix Halo and Windows stay off. The 780M's GPU can still reset on its own firmware (see Known limits); with the set on we saw no more resets than with it off, in small samples.
- **Strix Halo (gfx1151): the hipBLASLt tuning table is on.** The packaged Strix Halo engines (Linux `strixhalo` and the Windows `rdna3` package) use the table for their card when their hipBLASLt version matches it. The measurement is a community A/B from `bench/results/2026-10-05-community-gfx1151` (Linux, ROCm 7.17, hipBLASLt 1.5.0): prompts 250.9 to 528.9 tok/s (2.11x). We have no Strix Halo and did not repeat it. The table changes which matrix-product algorithm reads the prompt, so the answers are not bit-identical to plain hipBLAS (on an R9700 the first-token KL was 0.016, against a run-to-run difference of 0.00004; top-1 the same on 24 of 24 prompts). `STRATA_HIPBLASLT_TABLE=off` turns it off. On every other card the table is opt-in (`STRATA_HIPBLASLT_TABLE=on`): on the R9700 a table calibrated for the packaged hipBLASLt gave about +1% prompt and -2% decode, so none is shipped as a default. The tables are packaged per card (`tuning/` inside the engine package): Windows `rdna3` gfx1100 and gfx1151, Windows `hip` (RX 9000, R9700) gfx1201, Linux `rx7900` gfx1100, Linux `strixhalo` gfx1151; the Linux RX 9000 / R9700 package carries none, because no table matches its hipBLASLt. Only the gfx1151 table is used by default.
- **Two NVIDIA cards, several requests at once: one batch group.** With a layer split over exactly two NVIDIA cards and `--batch N`, the engine now runs one serial group instead of two pipelined groups. Measured on two RTX A4000 16 GB with Qwen3.8-Flash-Next IQ3_XXS, 5 interleaved pairs, aggregate tokens per second: 2 requests +15.9% (5 of 5 pairs), 4 requests +12.0% (5 of 5), 8 requests +14.7% (3 of 3). Every slot's tokens equal the solo run's, and the old default's, under the fixed identity flags (2 and 4 slots, 64 greedy tokens). A single request is not changed. It is not faster everywhere: when most hot experts sit in the CPU, as under the identity gate's small cache, the pipelined groups were about 10% faster (24.4 against 22.0 tok/s), so a card with a very small cache can lose here. `STRATA_BATCH_GROUPS_NV_SERIAL=0` restores the old default; `--batch-groups auto` or a number asks for the pipeline. AMD cards, three or more cards and the single-request paths are unchanged. On the final engine, 4 requests, 5 pairs: 78.06 against 65.97 tok/s (+18.3%, the old default faster in 0 of 5), and every slot's tokens equal the solo run's.
- **A card that draws no display keeps less in reserve.** The reserve of graphics memory the engine leaves free is now 512 MiB (700 MiB with pictures) on a card the probe says drives no screen (a compute-only card), instead of 1536 MiB. A card that drives a display keeps the 1536 / 2048 MiB safety default, and a number you set yourself (0 included) is always used as it is. Only the amount of free memory changes, so the answers are identical and the expert cache gets room for more experts. We did not time this ourselves: the report behind it (#3215) measured 80 against 50 tok/s with the forced reserve. Where the probe cannot tell (AMD and Intel on Linux) the safety default stays.
- **Packed models (`experts.bin`) on Linux: I/O prefetch and the decode gate are on when the page cache has room for at least 55% of the experts.** Measured on an RTX 3060 12 GB (Core Ultra 7 265), Qwen3.8-Flash-Next IQ3_XXS 43 GB pack with `--mmap-experts`, RAM limited to 32 GB by cgroup, cold page cache, 5 interleaved pairs: decode story / code / document 26.0 / 28.3 / 18.5 to 35.2 / 34.4 / 24.7 tok/s (x1.38 / x1.21 / x1.33, 5 of 5 pairs each), a 4K prompt x1.04 (4 of 5), a 20K prompt x1.06 (5 of 5). Same answers: the fixed-flag identity gate (10 prompts, 4K and 20K exact prompt checks) is identical with no RAM limit and with the 32 GB limit. With 16 GB of RAM the page cache holds 38% of the experts, so the default stays off: with it on, a cold 4K prompt read 4 to 6% slower. `STRATA_IO_PREFETCH=0` turns it off and `=1` forces it on. Linux only; only the IQ3_XXS pack was tested (not Q2_0, IQ3_S or Coder packs).
- **AMD RX 9000 / R9700 on Linux: the engine opens its GPU queues in a fixed order at start.** Before, about half of the fresh engines with MTP read prompts 8 to 14% slower, depending on which compute pipe the card's firmware gave the engine's two busiest queues (both on one pipe was slow). The engine now opens two queues on its main thread before anything else starts. Measured on two Radeon AI PRO R9700 boxes (Linux, ROCm 7.10, Q2_0 with MTP): without the fix 10 of 32 fresh starts read the 4K prompt under 2,000 tok/s (about 2,290 for a fast start); with it 0 of 32. Decode against the fix switched off, 20 interleaved rounds: 1.000 / 1.001 / 1.000 (story / code / facts). Opening more queues cost decode (five queues: 2 to 3.6% slower), so two is the default. Same answers: the identity gate (10 prompts, 4K and 20K exact checks) is identical for Q2_0 and IQ3_XXS, also with the 0.2.0 prompt defaults on. `STRATA_HIP_QUEUE_PRIME=0` turns it off. One card was measured; Windows and RX 7000 cards are not changed.
- **Linux hybrid CPUs with low-power E cores (Core Ultra "Meteor Lake" / "Arrow Lake-H", #3262).** The engine and setup now count the cores listed in `cpu_lowpower` as efficiency cores. A Core Ultra 7 255H used to look like 8 P and 8 E cores, so the hybrid plan did not apply and 15 workers ran; it now plans 10. The reporter measured the 15-worker default about 35% slower than 9. We have no such CPU and ran unit tests only (the plan and a fake `/sys`); only the number of workers changes, not the answers.
- **Two GPUs of different architectures (HIP): no start-up warm-up (#3204).** The warm-up product that runs on every card at start made prompts about 25% slower on a split of gfx1151 and gfx1201 for the reporter (`STRATA_PREFILL_WARM=0` restored them). It now runs only when every visible card has the same architecture. We have no mixed pair; on two R9700 (same architecture) the warm-up costs nothing (3,855 against 3,853 tok/s at a 32K prompt, 5 pairs), so the change leaves them as they were. The first request on a mixed pair pays the 1 to 2.5 s library load again, as before 0.2.0. `STRATA_PREFILL_WARM=1` / `0` overrides.
- **Linux, models read in place: a drive probe decides between the file cache and unbuffered reads (#3237).** The room rule picks the file cache when RAM seems to have room, which was 2x slower in prompts and 3 to 4x slower in decode for a reporter with a PCIe 5 drive (about 8 GB/s). When the rule says "cache" and the cache would hold under half of the reads, the engine now reads 96 random 1 MiB pieces both ways at start (under 2 s) and goes unbuffered only if the drive reads at least 4 GB/s and is faster that way. Every drive we have (1.6 to 3.1 GB/s) keeps the file cache; on a 2 GB/s NVMe the cache was better for decode (up to x1.6) and unbuffered reads better for prompts, the opposite of the report. Untested on a fast drive; the answers cannot change (only where reads go), and no identity gate was run. `STRATA_FILE_TIER_PROBE=0` turns it off.

## Fixes from user reports

- **Settings overwritten (#3215, #3270, #3216).** The app forced `--vram-reserve-mib` to 1536 (2048 with pictures) on every Load whatever your file said, which cut decode from 80 to 50 tok/s for one reporter, and a setup run that a Load started dropped every option it did not choose itself, control vectors included. Options set by hand are kept now and win over generated ones; an old file's hand edits are moved into `user_args`.
- **Choosing graphics cards (#3203, #3195, #3256, #3221, #3211).** Automatic no longer picks a card the engine has no code for (an AMD integrated GPU in front of a discrete card). One selected card is sent as a single card, not as a list the installer refuses. A card order from the settings file (`"gpu": [1,0]`, `"gpu_order": "as_given"`) is kept instead of being replaced by the app's own pick. The card list no longer ticks two cards with one click when two makes both count from 0. The dropdown rows fit long card names. The Monitor opens on the cards the model is assigned to.
- **Downloads (#3257, #3214, #3193).** The draft-layer download shows its progress in the app (it showed "0.0 / 0.0 GB"), runs again on a flaky link with fewer connections, and has one writer per folder. Cancelling, or a killed setup, now ends the whole process tree on Windows, so no orphan keeps writing. Gyro's low-RAM pack is written with `--compat-bf16`, which stopped the "command failed (exit 1): python.exe" at the packing step.
- **Re-download of a model you already have (#3199).** A model loaded from your own GGUF folder keeps that folder, so unloading and loading it again no longer downloads it a second time.
- **FP4-Local setup died at step 6 (#3227).** Setup now installs the pinned torch, transformers and safetensors the converter imports, before a prepare that needs them, and names a missing package at once instead of after 20 minutes.
- **The model stopped while starting (#3192).** A start that stopped because no graphics memory was left for the expert cache is tried once more with less kept free.
- **Crash on launch (Windows 11, exit code 0xC0000409, no log).** A failed start on Windows and Mac now leaves a log and a crash file in the app folder and shows a message box instead of closing. The reporter's own panic message is still unknown, so please send the new crash file if it happens again.
- **MTP, context and pictures setting kept coming back.** Every Load re-ran setup and rewrote them. A Load of an installed model is now direct, the picture-off choice sticks, a custom context size is shown and accepted, "MTP per request" is no longer frozen, and the new Draft layer switch is in Expert settings.
- **Your model library no longer moves.** `strata launch --data-dir` with a new folder used to move all existing models, packs and MTP files into it and rewrite your settings. It never moves them without asking now.
- **Math in the chat (#3268).** Formulas are drawn with KaTeX: `$...$` and `\(...\)` inline, `$$...$$` and `\[...\]` as blocks. KaTeX and its fonts ship with the app, load only when an answer has a formula, and work offline. Prices like "$5 and $10" and anything in code stay text. Checked with the formulas from the report in a browser.
- **Windows with a non-UTF-8 code page, such as Russian (#3202).** PowerShell output (the Documents folder, the save dialog, fonts, GPU names) was read in the wrong code page and came back as question marks; it is read as UTF-8 now. Python runs in UTF-8 mode from the launchers and the app's child processes. The engine and the picture reader carry a UTF-8 manifest, so a Cyrillic model folder arrives intact (Windows 10 1903 or newer). We reproduced the first two and tested the manifest with a small program; we could not run the engine on a Russian Windows, so a retest is welcome.
- **Install folder (#3186, #3190).** The Windows installer asks for the folder (another drive when C: is short). Updates and silent installs keep the earlier folder. The docs say what stays on C: (the engine bundle, settings and chats) and that `STRATA_COMPONENTS_DIR` moves the engine bundle. We compiled the page logic with NSIS on a reduced script; the full installer is built at release.
- **Linux engine killed with signal 9 and no out-of-memory (#3238).** A desktop with PipeWire and no rtkit can leave a finite `RLIMIT_RTTIME`. The server now warns at start when the limit is finite, and the engine-died message names it before the RAM hint. There is a troubleshooting entry.
- **Tools find `gguf-py` in the Control package (#3269).** `tools/iq_pack.py` also looks in the install folder (`STRATA_INSTALL_DIR`, the app folder); the error names `STRATA_GGUF_PY`.
- **Intel SYCL build (#3219).** `sycl/tools/build.sh` stops before the long compile when the `ocloc` of the base image is the one that crashes on the int8 kernels (Compute Runtime 26.22.38646.x, IGC 2.36.3) and says to `docker build --pull`; `STRATA_SYCL_I8_ESIMD=OFF` builds without those kernels (slower prompt experts, same answers). We could not reproduce the crash itself: a newer `ocloc` (26.31) builds the Battlemage target without errors.
- **gfx906 (MI50, Radeon Pro VII) builds again (#3172, #3271).** The Qwen3.6 engine is not built for it, the W4A4 target gets `GGML_USE_HIP`, and the trellis overlay and `moe_f16_kq` sources are in the HIP list. All 161 targets compile for gfx906 and `strata` links; we have no gfx906 card, so it was not run on one.
- **Trellis overlay with newer llama.cpp (#3217).** The overlay follows the signatures of the ggml-cuda it patches. On the pinned commit the generated files are byte-identical to before; against upstream 0ce8cd11 the old overlay failed to compile and the new one does.
- **Settings text (#3208).** "Allow browser origins" says it does nothing in the app (the app's API already allows pages of any site) and where `cors_origins` goes, in all eight languages.
- **Docs.** Build from git on Linux (#3191), the dual-socket CPU pool measurements, IOMMU check and no-numactl note (#3201; the NUMA-split pool from that report is not merged), and a two-card gfx906 tip with `--pipeline-windows 2` (+36% decode) and `--trim-stage-weights` (+5% prompt), measured by the reporter and off by default (#3173).

## Privacy

- Update checks run only when you click. Opening Settings, Engine and Update makes no network call; the last result is shown from your computer, and a new check starts only from the button. Offline, the check says "No internet connection. Strata works without it; try again when you are online."
- The assistant asks before it first searches the web or opens a web page. In Manual mode you are asked once per chat and the answer holds for that chat. Settings > Tools has a switch to skip the question (off by default), and a scheduled task cannot search unless you turned that on. Bypass mode does not ask.
- Starting, loading and chatting with a model on disk make no network calls. A test starts the host with every non-loopback request recorded and finds none. The old starter-model list can no longer download anything; it is display only.
- What Strata downloads and when is in `docs/SAFETY.md`.

## Known limits

- **Windows:** the installers are not code-signed yet, so Windows shows "Windows protected your PC": choose **More info**, then **Run anyway**.
- **Windows with an AMD card:** nothing has run on a real AMD card on Windows. The gfx12 prompt defaults and the 780M prompt set are off there. The Windows `rdna3` package (RX 7000 and Strix Halo) was built and scanned but not run on those cards by the maintainers.
- **Radeon 780M:** the GPU can reset with a firmware error (MES REMOVE_QUEUE) when the kernel moves memory the GPU uses. On our box the default engine lost 1 to 4 of 10 starts to it with or without the new prompt set, and the driver recovered each time. The firmware is the cause; we did not install new firmware.
- **Intel Arc Battlemage (B-series):** pictures stay opt-in. A first picture on a B70 once reset the card (xe driver); we could not repeat it on the A-series card and no B-series card was available for 0.2.1.
- **Mac:** the GPU picture reader was measured on an M4 only. The CPU reader is about 50 seconds per picture.
- **Strix Halo:** the hipBLASLt table default rests on a community measurement; please send the start-up line `hipBLASLt tuning table: ...` and a prompt run with the table on and off.
- **Docker:** the `rocm-gfx110x` and `rocm-gfx1151` images were not run on a card, and there is no Intel image.
- **AMD and Intel on Linux:** the engine cannot tell whether a card drives a display, so the safety reserve (1536 MiB) stays unless you set one.
- **Benchmark:** `strata bench run` implements the draft protocol; a first real run on a release engine is still to come.
- **Two NVIDIA cards, batch:** a card with a very small expert cache can be slower with one group than with two (see New defaults).
- **A100 (sm_80), #3252:** a report of decode -10% and prompts -20% since 0.1.45 was not reproduced. On a Tesla P100 (sm_60) and two RTX A4000 (sm_86) the 0.1.45 build against 0.1.44.1 measured decode x1.015 and x0.992, prompts x1.004 and x1.022 (5 interleaved rounds each), and the 0.2.1 tip is 7 to 10% faster in decode than 0.1.45 on both. Reading the commits found no sm_80-specific change. We have no A100; the reporter's numbers are needed.
- **Fast drives, #3237:** the drive probe above is proposed and untested on a drive over 4 GB/s.
- **NUMA-split CPU pool (#3201):** not part of 0.2.1; we have no dual-socket box to measure it.

Thanks to H3buss, who found that the Gyro import was missing `--compat-bf16` and where to put it (#3193); to bext1998, whose trace of the MTP download and the orphaned process (#3257) led to the progress and cancel fixes; and to Gazoo, who reported the card-selection, dropdown and re-download bugs (#3195, #3221, #3199). Thanks also to everyone who tested 0.2.0-beta and sent reports.

---

Strata is free and open source. If it runs well on your PC, a coffee keeps the work on it going:

<a href="https://buymeacoffee.com/strataengine"><img src="https://cdn.buymeacoffee.com/buttons/v2/default-yellow.png" alt="Buy Me A Coffee" height="50"></a>

name: Strata 0.2.0-beta
body: **0.2.0: Strata is now an app, a Terminal and an engine; installers that carry the engine; pictures on by default on NVIDIA and AMD cards; faster defaults for NVIDIA 12-16 GB cards, AMD RX 9000 / R9700 on Linux and Intel Arc.** Each new default below says whether the answers are identical to 0.1.45 (the identity gate) or change slightly, with the measured difference. Engine package version 0.1.45.3. Update with `strata update` (Terminal), Settings > Update (app), or `UPDATE.bat` / `./update.sh` (source installs). ## Which file to download | System | Your graphics card | File | | --- | --- | --- | | Windows 10 / 11 | NVIDIA RTX, driver 580 or newer | `Strata-0.2.0-beta-windows-cuda13.exe` | | | NVIDIA, older card or driver older than 580 | `Strata-0.2.0-beta-windows-cuda12.exe` | | | AMD Radeon RX 9000 series or Radeon AI PRO R9700 | `Strata-0.2.0-beta-windows-hip.exe` | | | AMD Radeon RX 7000 series or Ryzen AI Max (Strix Halo) | `Strata-0.2.0-beta-windows-hip-rdna3.exe` | | Linux | NVIDIA RTX, driver 580 or newer | `Strata-0.2.0-beta-linux-nvidia-cuda13.AppImage` | | | NVIDIA, older card or driver older than 580 | `Strata-0.2.0-beta-linux-nvidia-cuda12.AppImage` | | | AMD Radeon RX 9000 series or Radeon AI PRO R9700 | `Strata-0.2.0-beta-linux-amd-rx9070.AppImage` | | | AMD Radeon RX 7000 series | `Strata-0.2.0-beta-linux-amd-rx7900.AppImage` | | | AMD Ryzen AI Max (Strix Halo) | `Strata-0.2.0-beta-linux-amd-strixhalo.AppImage` | | Mac | Apple silicon, macOS 15 or newer | `Strata-0.2.0-beta-mac.dmg` (signed and notarised by Apple) | The Terminal installs with one line (below) and picks its engine by itself. The other files in this release are the engine and Terminal packages, the signed update feed and the in-app update files; you do not need to download them. ## Added after the first upload Two installers and two engines were added to this release later: `Strata-0.2.0-beta-windows-hip-rdna3.exe` (Windows, RX 7000 series and Ryzen AI Max; GPU code for gfx1100, gfx1101, gfx1102 and gfx1151; ROCm 10.2.0a20260930) and `Strata-0.2.0-beta-linux-amd-strixhalo.AppImage` (Linux, Ryzen AI Max; gfx1151; ROCm 7.14.1). The signed update feed is now sequence 101 and lists the two engine packages; `latest.json` and every other file are unchanged. Any other app installer works too: install it, then press **Update engine** in Settings (or run `strata update` in the Terminal) and the matching engine downloads. ## What is new **Three parts that share one engine.** - **The Strata app** for Windows (installer), Linux (AppImage) and Mac (Apple silicon, macOS 15 or newer, `.dmg`). Chat with a coding agent that asks before it acts (Manual) or works freely (Bypass), web search, `/loop`, pictures pasted or dropped into the chat, a Models page, a Storage page, a choice of which graphics cards a model uses, two models on two GPUs, sharing with other devices (needs an API key first) and setup of your coding apps. - **The Terminal**, one line to install (`curl -fsSL https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata/releases/latest/download/install.sh | sh`, `irm https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata/releases/latest/download/install.ps1 | iex` on Windows). `strata launch` is the guided flow (choose a model, tune it, serve it, watch it) and also runs without screens from flags; `strata connect` writes and checks the setup of OpenCode, Codex CLI, Claude Code, oh-my-pi, pi, Hermes Agent and OpenClaw; `strata models`, `strata update`, `strata doctor` and `strata bench run` are there too. The monitor `strata launch` opens has seven views, `1`-`7`, the seventh is Connect. See `docs/TERMINAL_LAUNCH.md`. - **The engine**, the part that talks to your card, is a separate package per platform and card. The installers carry one, so a new install starts a model without a download. Later engines come from a feed that is signed (Ed25519) and checked file by file, test-started before the switch and rolled back on any failure; models and saved tunings are never replaced. Update with `strata update` or Settings > Update. See `packaging/UPDATES.md` and `SECURITY.md`. - **A missing engine is a warning.** `strata launch` and the app say in plain words what is missing and what to do next, and still download the model. - Starting a model and serving never download anything; downloads are one explicit step. **Pictures are on by default on NVIDIA and AMD cards.** The picture reader runs on the CPU for a card under 24 GB (a few seconds per picture, nothing taken from the card) and on the graphics card from 24 GB. NVIDIA, AMD and Intel follow the same rule; `--vision gpu` / `--vision cpu` / off still choose per model. AMD now has a GPU reader with an automatic CPU fallback (the server prints one line when the GPU reader cannot start). Measured on a Radeon AI PRO R9700: a 260-token picture 57 ms on the GPU reader against 3.13 s on the CPU, a 972-token picture 0.40 s against 14.1 s; the GPU reader keeps 1,470 MiB of VRAM. On a Radeon 780M 0.40 s against 2.42 s. Gyro and the NVFP4 models read pictures too (Gyro needs engine 0.1.45.1 or newer). The Mac app has no picture reader yet. **Models.** Qwen3.6-35B-A3B has its three sizes in the app's catalog; the NVFP4 models have clear names. The app and `strata launch` now suggest a model by RAM and graphics memory together: 40 GB, Swift 1.5 IQ2_XS (or Gyro-M, slower); 48 GB, IQ3_XXS; 64 GB or more, IQ3_S (the original or Swift 1.5). With less memory, low-RAM mode starts by itself and the model runs slower. **Downloads are faster and checked.** Big files come over 8 connections at once (on the test PC 40 MB/s with one connection, 77 MB/s with eight) and continue where they stopped. Every model file has a fixed SHA-256 and size, and a download stops if the pinned version is gone from Hugging Face. Once a model is downloaded, Strata runs without internet. What Strata downloads and when is in `docs/SAFETY.md`. **The app's chat.** A finished page, document or picture opens in the sidebar by itself (the Open button opens it in your browser or default app). A chat without a chosen folder uses `Documents/Strata/Workspace`, so its files open and show in their folder. The first message no longer fails while the assistant's tools start, and sending with no model loaded says so. ## New defaults, with what we measured Every speed number below is a median of interleaved pairs against the previous default on the same box (a fresh engine per run); "pairs faster" counts the pairs the new default won. Each default has an off switch. - **NVIDIA RTX 30 / A-series (sm_86) and Pascal (sm_60): decode.** A per-architecture table of nine (sm_86) and seven (sm_60) switches, picked by removing one at a time and keeping only those that cost speed when removed. RTX 3060 12 GB 60.36 to 66.52 tok/s (+10.2%, 8 of 8 pairs), RTX A4000 16 GB 51.16 to 57.82 (+13.0%, 8 of 8), Tesla P100 16 GB 36.56 to 41.76 (+14.2%, 8 of 8). Same answers: the fixed-flag identity gate (10 prompts, 4K and 20K exact prompt checks) is identical on all three. `STRATA_SM86_PERF=0` / `STRATA_SM60_PERF=0` turn the table off. We left a prompt chunk above 8192 off on NVIDIA (not bit-exact on CUDA) and `STRATA_ROUTE_PRIOR=0.5` opt-in (KL 0.0126 against a run-to-run floor of 0.0012). - **AMD RX 9000 / R9700 (gfx12), Linux: prompt reading.** The WMMA prompt attention and the fused Q2_0 prompt experts are on. On an R9700 32 GB, Q2_0: a 4K prompt 1,151 to 2,286 tok/s and a 20K prompt 1,384 to 2,751 (1.99x, 5 of 5 pairs). IQ3_XXS: 4K 1,369 to 1,436 (1.05x), 20K 1,576 to 1,997 (1.27x). Decode is untouched (0.999 like for like, same tokens). The text changes slightly: teacher-forced KL 0.0003 (28 prompts) and 0.0015 (long documents), task suites equal; with both on: HumanEval 155/164, reasoning 27/30, agent 6/6, needles 6/6, tool calls 5/5. `STRATA_HIP_WMMA=0` and `STRATA_PF_FUSED=0` turn them off. On Windows they stay opt-in until tested there. - **Intel Arc A-series (Alchemist): prompt reading.** The XMX path (`STRATA_PF_XMX=2`) is the default. On an A750, 4K prompt 79.5 to 113.0 tok/s; by length (previous default / new) 1K 35.1 / 46.4, 2K 61.7 / 83.1, 6K 66.3 / 114.8. The logits equal those of the old opt-in; `STRATA_PF_XMX=0` brings back the previous default bit for bit. Not for Battlemage (it loses 7-11% there). - **Intel Arc A750: a prompt deadlock is fixed.** A prompt of about 5,000 tokens could hang the engine in the driver on pageable memory (the engine stopped, HTTP 503); the reproduction hung 6 of 6 before, completes 3 of 3 now, with identical first-token logits and needles 9 of 9 twice. - **Intel Arc B-series (Battlemage, B70): int8 experts for prompt reading.** On by default: 1K prompt 648 to 785 tok/s (+21%), 4K 1,264 to 1,419 (+12%), same output; `STRATA_PREFILL_MMQ=0` turns it off. Setup now picks an 8192 prompt chunk for a Battlemage card of 24 GB or more with a context over 32K: 16K prompt 1,222 to about 1,350 tok/s (+10-11%), 32K 1,187 to about 1,370 (+15-16%), decode unchanged. - **Linux, models read in place from the GGUF: RAM and SSD.** Zero-copy page-cached experts, I/O prefetch with a gate that checks it pays, and a RAM check that counts the container's clean page cache. On a 12 GB card emulated on a 72 GB card with the RAM limited by cgroup (Q2_0, three pairs): with 32 GB decode 1.70x / 2.56x / 2.88x, prompts 1.54x / 1.91x; with 16 GB decode 1.16x / 1.25x / 1.25x, prompts 1.63x / 1.68x; with an 18 GiB RAM tier decode 1.16x / 1.10x / 1.30x. On a real RTX 3060 the zero-copy part alone gave decode 1.14x / 1.44x / 1.47x. The gates are identical (Q2_0 and IQ3_S, with and without `--mmap-experts`). Packs in `experts.bin` keep the old behaviour. Off: `STRATA_COLD_OVERLAP=0`, `STRATA_IO_PREFETCH=0`, `STRATA_IO_PF_GATE=0`. - **The prompt chunk now accounts for RAM and SSD (file tier, Linux).** Where today's chunk would make the file set bigger than the page cache, the engine picks a smaller one. Measured on an RTX 3060 with the SATA SSD emulated (cgroup RAM limit and a 450 MB/s read limit, five pairs): a 20K prompt 334 to 822 tok/s (2.46x), a 29K prompt 419 to 910 (2.17x), drive reads for the 29K prompt 29.5 GB to 0.6 GB, decode after the prompt 28.6 to 45.7; a 4K prompt unchanged. Where the file set already fits the page cache (the 5070 test PC) it changes nothing. Tested on CUDA only. `STRATA_PREFILL_HOST_PLAN=0` turns it off. - **CPU worker counts follow the physical cores** (host socket, container quota, cap 32), and setup no longer writes half the logical threads (it wrote 128 on a 256-thread machine). Too many workers cost real speed: with as many workers as logical threads decode fell to 0.65-0.73 of the default on a 6-core and a 32-core box. Speed at the new defaults equals the old within noise (R9700, 31 to 30 workers: prompt 1.005-1.007, decode 1.000-1.007). A configured count above the plan still runs, with a warning. ## Fixes from the owner's tester reports - **Gyro-S gave empty or garbage answers on RTX 50 / RTX PRO (Blackwell).** The fused gate/up kernel assumed 80 dots per row and computed half of each row for Gyro's trellis types. Fixed; four test prompts failed before and pass now. Laurent Zuijdwijk's Gyro fork carries the same fix. - **Windows: a clean PC could not start the engine** (it needed `cublas64_13.dll` and `cublasLt64_13.dll`, which only a PC with the CUDA toolkit on its PATH had). Packages now carry every library they import, and a package that would miss one is refused when it is built. - **Linux and Mac: the agent chat never started** (a pruning rule removed a Harness package it imports on every system). - **Storage "Check folder" unloaded the models;** only a real change of folder does now. - **The app showed the engine's version as the app version** in Settings > Update. - **Qwen3.6 showed no sizes** in the catalog and the first-run page. - **A folder from an old settings file (`T:\Strata`) was adopted as the install folder.** The app passes its own folder now. - **Downloads:** one progress bar for the model and its picture reader, choices kept when you switch tabs. - **Web search** stopped after the third search when DuckDuckGo refused; it falls back to another search source and waits before asking DuckDuckGo again. A turn that loops on failed searches, or runs out of context, now ends cleanly and says why. - **`/loop`** can be stopped by a count, a time or the answer ("stop after 3 answers"). - **Anthropic base URL:** the app and `strata connect` show the address without `/v1`; a pasted `/v1` is cut back. - **Files edited:** the chat no longer lists files it did not touch after a turn. - **Cloudflare tunnel:** `cloudflared` is found on your PATH and in the usual places, and a copy that is already running is not started twice. - **Terminal:** flags no longer crash the start screen; `strata models` finds models the app installed; no web page opens by itself; `strata connect --check --output json` prints one JSON object and exits 1 when a check failed. ## Known limits - **Mac:** no picture reader yet; macOS 15 or newer. The app and the Terminal are signed and notarised by Apple. - **Windows:** the installers are not code-signed yet, so Windows shows "Windows protected your PC": choose **More info**, then **Run anyway**. - **Windows with an AMD card:** the installer and the GPU picture reader are built, but nothing has run on a real AMD card on Windows. The gfx12 prompt defaults are opt-in there. - **AMD RX 7000 (gfx1100-1102) and Strix Halo (gfx1151):** the packages are built, linked and scanned (library imports, file hashes, the GPU code inside each binary, `--version` in a clean environment, a clean refusal of the Linux packages on an RX 9000 card, update-feed selection tests). The maintainers have not run them on an RX 7000 or a Strix Halo card. What other people ran: an RX 7900 XTX on Windows 11 ran the earlier ready-made Windows engine (0.1.40, report #1173), and Strix Halo owners ran Linux builds made from source on the ROCm 7.14 line (`bench/results/COMMUNITY.md`). Nobody has run Strix Halo on Windows. The packaged AMD engines do not carry the hipBLASLt tuning tables yet (planned for 0.2.1), so prompt reading is slower than the source-build numbers in [STRIX_HALO.md](STRIX_HALO.md) and [AMD_HIP.md](AMD_HIP.md). - **Mini PCs with a Radeon 780M / 880M / 890M:** the matrix-core prompt defaults are parked. On the 780M the GPU reset (MES REMOVE_QUEUE) when they were tried; the iGPU keeps its opt-in switches. - **R9700:** about half of the fresh engines with MTP read prompts 10-23% slower than the others (4K: about 1,350 instead of 1,700 tok/s). Not seen on NVIDIA; the cause is not found. - **Docker images are not published yet;** build them yourself (`docs/DOCKER.md`). - **`strata code` is not available** in the Terminal; use `strata connect` for coding apps (the app has its own agent). - The standard benchmark protocol is a draft (`docs/BENCHMARK_PROTOCOL.md`); `strata bench run` and `BENCH.bat` do not implement it. Thanks to Laurent Zuijdwijk (the Gyro kernels for CPU and the trellis types), ATIVX928 and NoxestNoz (Volta work) and everyone who tested the builds and sent reports. --- Strata is free and open source. If it runs well on your PC, a coffee keeps the work on it going:

name: Strata 0.1.45
body: **0.1.45: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B reads pictures, serves several requests at once and runs up to 40% faster; switches for multi-user servers; Mac and setup fixes.** Answers of the Qwen3.8-Flash-Next models are the same as in 0.1.44.1 (byte-identical in our identity tests on every GPU machine we tested: CUDA sm_60 / sm_86, HIP gfx1201, Intel A750, Mac M4). Update with `UPDATE.bat` (Linux: `./update.sh`); setup replaces the engine with 0.1.45. ## Qwen3.6-35B-A3B - **Pictures.** Setup asks "Do you want images?" for Qwen3.6, downloads the pinned `mmproj` (0.9 GB) and writes `--vision`. It is the same projector family as Flash-Next's, so the same image encoder reads it. Checked against llama.cpp on the same pictures, same prompt ids, teacher-forced on llama.cpp's own answer: first token the same in 5 of 6 cases (the sixth, two pictures in one request, differs at a near tie), mean KL 0.0005 to 0.035 against 0.002 to 0.056 between llama.cpp's own CPU and GPU runs. Answers on the test pictures are the same text llama.cpp gives. - **Several requests at once** (`--parallel N` at setup, `"parallel": N` in the config, up to 8). Every window carries one token of each conversation, so the dense weights and every expert two conversations share are read once. Every slot decodes the tokens it decodes alone (10 prompts x 128 greedy, 2 / 4 / 8 slots, slots reused, a 2.5K-token prompt read beside decoding slots). An R9700 32 GB with every expert in VRAM, 128 new tokens per request, five interleaved pairs against llama.cpp's `llama-server -np N -fa on`: 1 / 2 / 4 / 8 requests 83.9 / 173.5 / 252 / 325 tok/s against 73.8 / 107 / 165 / 208 (1.14x to 1.61x, 5 of 5 pairs each). `--batch-mtp` (opt-in) lets every slot verify draft tokens: one request 1.6x, two 1.2x, four 1.1x. - **Setup offers it, with the price.** Where every expert stays in VRAM, setup suggests up to 3-4 slots. On a card that does not hold every expert the slots take VRAM from the expert cache: a request alone runs 4-11% slower, and next to one request at a time WITH the draft layer, N together are only 1.0-1.15x faster (RTX 3060 12 GB at 8K context, 4 requests: 1.15x, alone -4%; RTX A4000 / Tesla P100 16 GB at 32K, 2 requests: 1.0x, alone -7 to -11%). Setup says that, offers the count the card can spare at the chosen context (12 GB: 4 slots at 8K, none at 32K; 16 GB: 2 at 32K), asks "How many requests at once?" (Enter keeps one at a time) and keeps any number you give. It is worth it for several users or agents at once, not for one chat. - **Faster.** New decode kernels with the old kernels' bits (checked on the real activations: 0 mismatches in 18,360 comparisons), a prompt delta rule that loads one token ahead, and a bigger prompt chunk by default (4096 / 2048 / 1024 tokens, whatever fits; `--prefill 512` brings the old one back). R9700 32 GB, UD-Q4_K_XL: decode 83.2 to 117.8 tok/s (1.42x, 5 of 5 pairs; llama.cpp 82), 4K prompt 3,453 to 6,220 tok/s (1.80x), with `--mtp 2` 167.7 to 183.7. UD-Q6_K_XL: decode 80.4 to 106.9.
